text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Generative AI and photo data use lack required review","detail":"The proposal generates instructions from past pickup photos, which is generative AI and may involve personal data (people, plates, faces in photos). No legal, privacy, or AI governance review is recorded; only a data dependency on the store systems team is listed.","evidence_quote":"Generate store-specific pickup instructions from past pickup photos and show them in the driver app.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Record privacy/legal and generative AI policy reviews, covering photo PII handling, content accuracy checks, and approval before launch."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Non-random assignment and short duration","detail":"Markets are self-selected by volunteering managers and compared with the rest, which introduces selection bias and confounding. The 3-week duration is above the 14-day minimum, but the 10-week metric target does not match it. The MDE of 1 point is also unclear relative to the metrics (Cost Per Delivery is in dollars, so a 1-point MDE is unitless and inconsistent with the $0.15 target).","evidence_quote":"Run a pilot in the markets whose managers volunteer and compare against the remaining markets. Duration: 3 weeks. MDE: 1 point, power 80%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Randomize at an appropriate unit (stores or markets) with matched controls, specify MDE in the primary metric's units with a power calculation, and align the experiment duration with the target timeframe."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing guardrails for pickup flow changes","detail":"The change affects driver behavior at pickup, but the only guardrail is Delivery Defect Rate. Metrics such as pickup wait or dwell time, on-time delivery rate, and driver experience or safety are absent, and a defect-rate guardrail alone won't capture slower or confusing pickups.","evidence_quote":"Delivery Defect Rate: stop if it rises by more than 0.2 points.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails for pickup dwell time, on-time delivery rate, driver support contacts, and instruction accuracy or error reports."},{"type":"NO_BASELINE_TARGET","title":"Success metric not tied to the problem","detail":"The stated problem is drivers who cannot find the pickup counter and the associate time spent on it. The success metric is Cost Per Delivery, which is a distant outcome, and the 10-week timeframe is inconsistent with the 3-week experiment, so the target can't be validated by it. There is no direct metric for the problem (e.g., time to find the counter, associate interruptions).","evidence_quote":"Cost Per Delivery: from $7.40 to $7.25 within 10 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add a direct success metric with baseline, target, and timeframe (e.g., pickup search time or associate interruptions per shift), and align the measurement window with the experiment."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Problem claim lacks specific quantification and cost baseline source","detail":"The cost baseline of $7.40 has no stated source, and the survey is cited without any figures on how much associate time is spent. The claimed benefit of $0.15 per delivery has no supporting rationale.","evidence_quote":"from $7.40 to $7.25","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite the source for the $7.40 baseline and provide an estimate linking the instruction feature to the $0.15 reduction."}]}
